before: Backticks in a type can describe string patterns. Here ${Topic} inserts each member of the finite Topic union, producing exactly "goal:saved" | "note:saved". The interpolation is a type operation, not a string-building function.

eventLabel receives one EventName and returns a string with the Received prefix. The colon and saved text are literal parts of each accepted name. These types are erased: text arriving from a file or network still needs runtime validation rather than a type assertion pretending it was checked.
Optional local practice: Add a third Topic and predict the extra accepted event string.
after: A template literal type describes text using backticks. `${Topic}` places each allowed topic into the pattern. With topics `"goal"` and `"note"`, the pattern allows `"goal:saved"` and `"note:saved"`.
The ending `:saved` is part of the rule. `"goal:deleted"` does not fit. This type describes allowed text; it does not build a new text value while the program runs.
Define `EventName` using `Topic` and the exact ending `:saved`. Complete `eventLabel` to add `"Received "` before the event name.

These type rules are removed before the program runs. Text from a file or the internet still needs a real check. Adding `"photo"` to `Topic` would allow `"photo:saved"`, but it would not make all photo-related text valid.
